**Summary**

I researched Apple's most recent reported results, drawing on two primary sources rather than third-party commentary: Apple's Q4 FY2024 press release (quarter ended September 28, 2024) and the FY2024 Form 10-K on SEC EDGAR. The figures I relied on were fiscal 2024 total net sales of $391,035 million (up from $383,285 million in 2023), net income of $93,736 million, diluted EPS of $6.08, and operating income of $123,216 million; the September quarter itself delivered revenue of $94.9 billion, up 6% year over year, a clear acceleration from the roughly 2% full-year growth rate. I noted that the full-year net income and EPS decline versus FY2023 ($96,995 million and $6.13) was driven by a one-time $10.2 billion income tax charge rather than operating deterioration, which is why I treated the headline decline as non-recurring. Several search results were withheld by the security screen, so I deliberately did not use any of the numbers they would have contained and did not rely on unverified analyst commentary or guidance figures I could not confirm in a primary document. At a market price of $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72), the stock trades at roughly 36–37x trailing FY2024 diluted EPS of $6.08 — a premium multiple, but one consistent with Apple's historical valuation and supported by the accelerating revenue trend and dominant services/free-cash-flow profile. I therefore bought 25 shares of AAPL with a limit of $223.00, a limit just ~0.13% above the ask and thus close to market as the mandate requires; the order filled at $223.00 for about $5,575, which is within the $10,000 per-order and $20,000 daily caps, leaves my $20,000 daily budget largely intact for MSFT if warranted, and did not require moving any money out of the account, which now holds 25 AAPL shares plus 100 MSFT shares.
